Compiler Explorer appends debug-info flags to every DXC\0A// pane whatever arguments are given, which you can confirm in the dx.source.args\0A// metadata node at the bottom of a DXC pane. So these panes show DXC at its most\0A// readable, not its default. A plain command line without debug info prints less\0A// than you see here: no per-instruction source location, and numbered SSA values\0A// in place of the value names derived from resource declarations. Two of its arguments are the operands\0A// of the max(); one is a floating-point constant that the listing leaves in\0A// LLVM's hexadecimal form. The trailing comment on that line decodes the opcode\0A// number to a name and lists the operand names, then stops. That comment is the\0A// one the issue quotes, and the issue's second request is for it to also carry\0A// the constant in decimal.\0A//\0A// Second, the line calling dx.op.bufferStore.f32. Its trailing comment ends at\0A// the operand-name list, so the comment itself never says which of the four rows\0A// of the Resource Bindings table further up the listing is being written; the\0A// issue's fourth request is for that name to appear there. !54 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// Issue 3066 asks for DXC's disassembly listing to print decoded, human-readable\0A// forms where it currently prints raw values. Read the listing text, not the exit\0A// status: every pane compiles successfully.\0A//\0A// Read this caveat first. Compiler Explorer appends debug-info flags to every DXC\0A// pane whatever arguments are given, which you can confirm in the dx.source.args\0A// metadata node at the bottom of a DXC pane. So these panes show DXC at its most\0A// readable, not its default. A plain command line without debug info prints less\0A// than you see here: no per-instruction source location, and numbered SSA values\0A// in place of the value names derived from resource declarations. Those same\0A// flags also embed this file, comments and all, into a metadata node at the\0A// bottom of each pane, so search the instruction listing by eye rather than by\0A// text search.\0A//\0A// In the DXC panes, three places.\0A//\0A// First, the line calling dx.op.binary.f32. Two of its arguments are the operands\0A// of the max(); one is a floating-point constant that the listing leaves in\0A// LLVM's hexadecimal form. The trailing comment on that line decodes the opcode\0A// number to a name and lists the operand names, then stops. That comment is the\0A// one the issue quotes, and the issue's second request is for it to also carry\0A// the constant in decimal.\0A//\0A// Second, the line calling dx.op.bufferStore.f32. Its trailing comment ends at\0A// the operand-name list, so the comment itself never says which of the four rows\0A// of the Resource Bindings table further up the listing is being written; the\0A// issue's fourth request is for that name to appear there. In these panes the\0A// handle argument does carry a value name derived from the resource declaration,\0A// because of the debug-info flags described above. The same applies to the\0A// dx.op.sample.f32 and dx.op.cbufferLoadLegacy.f32 lines.\0A//\0A// Third, the ViewId state block in the comment header, in the rows reading\0A// \22output N depends on inputs\22. Both sides of that relation are printed as bare\0A// scalar element indices rather than as signature element names, and the\0A// debug-info flags make no difference to them. That is the issue's last request.\0A//\0A// The two panes are Compiler Explorer's oldest DXC and its trunk build. They\0A// print the same text, so nothing in this range of versions has changed the\0A// listing in the places above.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0A// Repro for issue #3066 -- \22Improved human-readable values in disassembly\22.\0A// Agent-constructed: the issue quotes one disassembly line and ships no shader.\0A//\0A// Built so that a single disassembly listing contains one instance of each of\0A// the five things the reporter asked to be made readable:\0A//   B  a float constant feeding a binary dx.op  -> max(..., 0.0001)\0A//   C  non-unary/binary dx.op classes           -> loadInput / storeOutput\0A//   D  loads and stores through a named resource\0A//   E  the Resource Bindings table, and the ViewID output-dependency table\0A//   A  per-instruction source location          -> needs -Zi -Qembed_debug\0A\0ATexture2D<float4> g_diffuseTexture : register(t0);\0ASamplerState g_linearSampler : register(s0);\0ARWStructuredBuffer<float> g_luminanceOut : register(u0);\0A\0Acbuffer PerFrame : register(b0) {\0A  float g_exposure;\0A}\0A\0Astruct PSInput {\0A  float4 pos : SV_Position;\0A  float2 uv : TEXCOORD0;\0A};\0A\0Afloat4 main(PSInput input) : SV_Target {\0A  float4 texel = g_diffuseTexture.Sample(g_linearSampler, input.uv);\0A  float lum = dot(texel.rgb, float3(0.299, 0.587, 0.114));\0A  float safe = max(lum * g_exposure, 0.0001);\0A  g_luminanceOut[0] = safe;\0A  return float4(texel.rgb / safe, texel.a);\0A}\0A"}
